venue_analysis.downtown_linden_corner: Cafe, $. Meat-free board, peanut-safe (deskmate with auto-injector eats the whole menu), dairy-free by default (oat latte, olive oil, white-bean soup), fresh and light. Meets every constraint: 3 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_slate_window: Thick satay dressing on every grain bowl and in-house roasted peanuts. Fails Cyrus's peanut allergy: 0 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_wren_house: Every dish has meat or fish. Fails Mina's vegetarian diet: 0 stars.
venue_analysis.downtown_paper_kite: Peanut-safe, light and healthy, half the menu vegetarian, but cheese, cream, butter and whole milk everywhere. Roxy's dairy intolerance costs a star: 2 stars (maybe fewer if half a meat-free menu doesn't meet the 'sushi day' bar).
venue_analysis.downtown_marble_steps: Peanut-safe and dairy-safe, but the food is heavy and fried. Misses Brooke's wholesome request: 2 stars at best. It's also unclear whether the rest of the menu is vegetarian.

notes: Fair and solvable. Each decoy fails exactly one constraint, and the clues are indirect but readable: the satay plus emergency pen means peanuts, 'stomach not speaking' to milk, butter and cheese means a dairy intolerance, and sushi day means vegetarian. Small point: Linden Corner never says outright that its whole menu is meat-free. You have to infer it from 'went meat-free... never felt like a sacrifice... still working through the board'. That matches the 'sushi day standard' clue, but it's softer than the explicit wording on the other cards. Paper Kite's 'half the board is meat-free' puts the line between 'the menu has vegetarian options' and 'the whole menu is safe' to the test, and a first-time player could stop to think about it. Nothing unfair or contradictory.
